# Microsoft Ads Cost in 2026: Bing Ads Pricing and Budget

Paid Search

•

September 14, 2026

Read More

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/66a7ce7cd5c9fd8083f11740/66fc214ef5d7bfc029b0f9de_T061ENXEC-U06C5SGG597-12b2dab7356a-512.avif)

Anastasiya Khvin



](https://aimers.io/author/anastasiya-khvin)

![Bing Ads Cost](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/66a7ce7cd5c9fd8083f11740/67fce050a25b88328d34fba6_Bing%20Ads%20Cost%20in%202025_%20Is%20It%20Worth%20It.avif)

Imagine paying less for your ads - and still reaching high-intent searchers who are ready to convert. Sounds like a dream, right? But for smart marketers in 2026, it might just be a Bing thing.

With Google Ads getting more competitive (and expensive) by the month, many companies are turning to Bing Ads (now Microsoft Advertising) to stretch their ad dollars further. But how much does Bing advertising actually cost? And is it worth it?

**Terminology note:** Bing Ads was renamed Microsoft Advertising. This guide uses **Microsoft Ads** for the platform and **Bing Ads cost** where it helps match the way marketers still search for pricing information.

Let's break down the numbers, look at how Bing compares to Google, and show you how to get the most out of your Bing Ads budget.

## Microsoft Ads Cost in 2026: The Short Answer

**Microsoft Ads does not have a fixed price or a required minimum spend.** For search campaigns, advertisers set bids and daily budgets, then typically pay when someone clicks. Your actual CPC is determined by the auction, so the useful answer is a range from your own forecast and account data - not one platform-wide average.

For current directional context, [**Microsoft says advertisers can get 19% lower CPCs and 6% higher CTRs**](https://ads.microsoft.com/) than a leading ad platform, citing an eMarketer Q1 2026 forecast. Treat that as a platform-level comparison, not a guaranteed result for every keyword, country, or account. A 2025 agency benchmark placed average Microsoft Ads CPC around $1.50-$2.80, but third-party ranges should only be used as a planning reference.

Benchmark source: [QueryClick's 2025 paid media benchmark](https://queryclick.com/insights/what-does-best-in-class-paid-media-look-like-in-the-age-of-ai-serps/). Microsoft does not present that range as a guaranteed platform average.

The practical takeaway: build your budget from expected CPC, required click volume, landing-page conversion rate, and target CPA. For B2B teams, this channel can add efficient high-intent reach alongside [digital marketing for B2B tech companies](https://aimers.io/industries/tech-digital-marketing-agency) - but it should be evaluated on qualified pipeline, not cheap clicks alone.

## How Microsoft Ads Pricing Works

Microsoft Search ads run through an auction. Your bid matters, but the highest bidder does not automatically win the best position. Ad relevance, expected performance, landing-page experience, competition, and campaign settings can all affect delivery and cost.

*   **Manual CPC:** you control keyword bids directly and can use it for tightly managed tests.
*   **Enhanced CPC and automated bidding:** Microsoft adjusts bids toward the selected goal, using the conversion signals available to the campaign.
*   **Target CPA or Maximize Conversions:** these strategies need accurate conversion tracking and enough conversion volume to learn. [Microsoft's automated bidding guidance](https://help.ads.microsoft.com/apex/index/3/en/56786) recommends at least 30 conversions in the previous 30 days before evaluation, followed by a one- to two-week learning period.

Search ads can appear across Bing and [Microsoft search partners](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/solutions/ad-products-formats/search), which may include Yahoo, AOL, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, and other partner inventory. Review network performance instead of assuming every placement has the same CPC or lead quality. For campaign-format guidance, see Aimers' [Microsoft Ads campaign types for B2B SaaS](https://aimers.io/blog/best-microsoft-ads-campaign-types-for-b2b-saas).

## How Much Should You Budget for Microsoft Ads?

There is no platform minimum, but a budget can still be too small to answer the business question. Start with the amount of evidence you need, then work backward from CPC and conversion assumptions.

| Planning scenario | Simple formula | Example only | What it tells you |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Initial keyword validation** | **Expected CPC x 100 clicks** | **$3 CPC x 100 = $300** | **Whether queries, CTR, and early engagement look relevant.** |
| **Search conversion pilot** | **Expected CPC x 200 clicks** | **$5 CPC x 200 = $1,000** | **An early conversion-rate signal; still weak for long B2B sales cycles.** |
| **Target CPA planning** | **Target CPA x required conversions** | **$150 CPA x 30 = $4,500** | **A budget aligned with enough conversion volume to assess automation.** |
| **Pipeline planning** | **Target customers / close rate / SQL rate / lead rate x expected CPC** | **Use your funnel rates** | **Whether the channel can support revenue goals, not just lead volume.** |

At Aimers, we generally recommend around **$3,000 per month per platform** as a practical starting point for meaningful SaaS and tech testing when search volume and unit economics support it. That is an agency planning recommendation, not a Microsoft minimum. A [Bing Ads management](https://aimers.io/services/bing-ads-agency) plan should still be sized around your market, sales cycle, conversion rates, and qualified-pipeline target.

## Bing Ads CPC by Industry and Use Case

Published industry averages are useful for orientation, but broad categories hide the biggest cost drivers: keyword intent, geography, match type, competition, and conversion quality. Use the table below as a relative planning guide, then replace it with your own forecast.

| Use case | Typical pressure | Why | Budget implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Brand search** | **Low to medium** | **High relevance and limited direct competition.** | **Protect coverage, but check incrementality and organic overlap.** |
| **Niche B2B long-tail** | **Low to medium** | **Lower query volume and fewer bidders.** | **Expect efficient clicks but limited scale.** |
| **Non-brand SaaS category** | **Medium to high** | **Multiple vendors compete for demo and comparison intent.** | **Prioritize qualified terms and landing-page relevance.** |

# Bing Paid Advertising: How It Works and Compares to Google Ads

KME.digital

7 May 2025

Although many marketing professionals treat Google Ads as their first and primary paid digital advertising platform, it is far from the only option. Microsoft Advertising, formerly Bing Ads, has also become a strategic channel for organizations that cater to B2B and B2G professionals. Although the functionality and reach of [Microsoft Advertising pay-per-click (PPC) campaigns](https://kme.digital/ppc-management/) diverge in crucial ways from Google’s, these distinctions can power new growth at your organization. Specifically, they encourage brand awareness, generate leads, and engage decision-makers through previously untargeted channels.

Washington, DC, business owners looking to maximize their digital reach can rely on KME.digital for expert support across both Google and Microsoft advertising platforms. From strategic keyword targeting to campaign optimization and performance tracking, our digital marketing team has deep experience managing paid media that applies it to drive measurable results. Call (703) 585-3321 to [learn how we can fine-tune your digital marketing strategy](https://kme.digital/contact-us/).

Below, we explore paid advertising opportunities on Bing, particularly how its platform differs from Google Ads: 

## What is Microsoft Advertising?

[Microsoft Advertising](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/solutions/ad-products-formats/search?s_cid=en-us-acq-pm-src_ggl-sub_gglsb&ef_id=_k_Cj0KCQjw8cHABhC-ARIsAJnY12xFCsVtdBgWogTzAEhmeBgOyxlkkpXthClXIK4qiuz17kJnQvRmdLAaAoe_EALw_wcB_k_&OCID=AIDcmmkmesoutg_SEM__k_Cj0KCQjw8cHABhC-ARIsAJnY12xFCsVtdBgWogTzAEhmeBgOyxlkkpXthClXIK4qiuz17kJnQvRmdLAaAoe_EALw_wcB_k_&gad_source=1&gbraid=0AAAAADcJh_tf9OFeGNGJp_S9MsZZc4c3l&gclid=Cj0KCQjw8cHABhC-ARIsAJnY12xFCsVtdBgWogTzAEhmeBgOyxlkkpXthClXIK4qiuz17kJnQvRmdLAaAoe_EALw_wcB#ad-extensions) is a pay-per-click (PPC) platform that places ads across the Microsoft Search Network, including Bing, Yahoo, AOL, and other partner websites. Like Google Ads, it allows advertisers to bid on keywords, create ad campaigns, and [reach users through search engine results pages (SERPs)](https://kme.digital/the-value-of-seo-vs-paid-ads-marketing/). However, the platform’s proprietary placement in Microsoft’s ecosystem (including LinkedIn, MSN, and Windows devices) offers ad-targeting capabilities that other platforms cannot match.

## Microsoft Advertising’s Capabilities vs. Google Ads’

*   **User Interface & Tools**While both platforms have intuitive user interfaces and campaign-building tools, Microsoft Advertising provides a streamlined, user-friendly design that simplifies campaign creation and management. Its powerful features include AI-driven recommendations, predictive targeting, and advanced reporting tools, which enable real-time optimizations based on actionable insights. Additionally, [Microsoft’s interface offers customization options for reporting](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/blog/post/march-2022/reporting-made-easier-with-microsoft-advertising#:~:text=Once%20you've%20signed%20in,less%20time%20on%20routine%20tasks.), which empowers marketers to track key performance metrics tailored to their specific goals.  
      
    Google offers similar functionality through Google Ads and Google Analytics. Users can create and manage campaigns, access basic audience targeting options, and view performance data. Google Ads also supports multiple ad formats and provides standard tools for tracking conversions and measuring campaign results.  
    
*   **Integrations & Partnerships**  
    Microsoft Advertising gives users access to a wide audience thanks to the company’s powerful and integrated ecosystem. Your ads can reach Windows PC, Microsoft Edge, Outlook, Office, Xbox, and LinkedIn users – many of which professionals and consumers utilize daily. Furthermore, Microsoft ads can reach [search engines like Yahoo and DuckDuckGo because Bing powers searches on these portals](https://kme.digital/why-your-organization-should-pursue-bing-search-engine-marketing/). With the addition of OpenAI’s ChatGPT to Bing, Microsoft has enhanced the search experience and extended its influence to a global user base.
    
    Although Google Ads’ reach includes popular platforms like YouTube and Google’s display network, Microsoft Advertising stands out thanks to the professional orientation of its customer base. If you’re targeting corporate or government buyers, Microsoft offers the strategic advantage you need to make meaningful connections.
    
*   **Demographic Segmentation**  
    Both Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising offer demographic segmentation, allowing advertisers to target audiences based on age, gender, income level, geographic location, and other factors. These capabilities enable you to tailor campaigns to specific market segments, whether general consumers or more defined audience groups. Google Ads also includes [behavioral targeting through in-market audiences](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2497941?hl=en), which works well for broad B2C reach but is less precise for professional targeting.
    
    Microsoft Advertising, however, goes a step further by combining standard demographic filters with exclusive access to LinkedIn profile data. This integration allows you to target users based on professional attributes, giving you a strategic advantage when marketing to corporate and government decision-makers.
    

## The Unique Benefits of Microsoft Paid Advertising![pay per click advertising in Washington DC](/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image1-1024x576.jpg)

Although Microsoft Advertising offers the greatest value for [businesses targeting government buyers](https://kme.digital/government-capture-and-proposal-services-with-integrated-marketing/) or corporate decision-makers, it can also enhance advertisers’ efforts when applied strategically. The platform’s compelling benefits include:

*   **Low CPC and Competition  
    **Since fewer businesses advertise on Microsoft’s network than on Google, those that do enjoy lower cost-per-click (CPC) rates and less competition for high-value keywords. Indeed, [Microsoft Advertising’s CPC hovers around $1.54](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2017/11/06/bing-ads-perfor

## Which offers better ROI for small businesses: Bing Ads or Google Ads?

For most small businesses, Google Ads should come first because it carries far more search demand, and Microsoft Advertising (Bing Ads) is a logical second platform to test once Google is profitable, but which one returns more per dollar for your business depends on cost per customer, not cost per click.

The volume gap is large. In August 2026, StatCounter put Google’s US search engine market share at 86.1% and Bing’s at 8.92% ([StatCounter, August 2026](https://gs.statcounter.com/search-engine-market-share/all/united-states-of-america)). Microsoft’s reach is stronger on desktop: its advertising site cites 109 million unique US PC users and a 38.1% US PC search market share, based on Comscore desktop-only data from March 2023 ([Microsoft Advertising](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/solutions/ad-products-formats/search)). A cheaper click on Bing only matters if the customers it brings cost less too, so this 16-account study reports CPC in “Is Bing Ads Cheaper Than Google Ads?” and then asks whether cheaper traffic means cheaper customers in “Does Cheaper Traffic Mean Cheaper Customers?” below.

| Your situation | Where to start | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New to paid search, one small budget, need leads soon | Google Ads | Most search volume, so you learn which keywords convert fastest |
| Very few conversions a month | Google only, for now | Splitting thin data across two platforms slows learning on both |
| Google campaigns profitable but limited by volume | Add Microsoft Advertising | Copy proven campaigns across with [Google Import](https://hustlemarketers.com/import-google-ads-to-microsoft-ads/), then tune bids |
| B2B or desktop-heavy buyers | Test Microsoft Advertising early | Desktop reach and [LinkedIn profile targeting](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/solutions/audience-targeting/linkedin-profile-targeting) by company, industry or job function |
| Both running | Move budget by cost per conversion | Keep what converts cheaper per customer, not per click |

A starting split, as practitioner guidance rather than a benchmark: when you add Microsoft Advertising, give it a small share of the search budget at first, for example 10 to 20 percent, then shift money toward whichever platform has the lower cost per conversion after a full month of data.
